title: Micro-Canary Lightweight Checklist + Two-Week Rollout Calendar (Mar 2026) - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, low-friction canary checklist + two-week rollout calendar for a minor runtime improvement (v1.3.2) that changes batching heuristics and adds a telemetry toggle. Goal: validate in prod with minimal blast radius, gather cost/latency delta, and ship release notes.

Scope:
- Applies only to hosted and dedicated clusters in us-west1 and eu-west1 for the initial canary phase.
- Private/VPC deployments handled by a separate ops runbook (not covered here).
- Rollout is a micro-canary: start with 2% traffic, scale to 25% over two weeks if metrics are healthy.

Quick TL;DR rollout plan (summary):
- Day 0 (preflight): run smoke on staging; sanity metrics; canary image bake.
- Day 1: 2% production traffic in us-west1 for 6 hours -> evaluate.
- Day 2-3: hold and observe; optional rollback if regressed.
- Day 4: expand to 10% us-west1 and 2% eu-west1 for 24 hours.
- Day 7: expand to 25% global (split across regions).
- Day 14: full rollout if all gates pass.

Two-Week Calendar (compact):
- 2026-03-04: Preflight checklist + staging smoke (owner: Priya)
- 2026-03-05: Canary deploy 2% us-west1 09:00-15:00 PT (owner: Samir)
- 2026-03-06: Observability review 10:00 PT (owner: Hannah)
- 2026-03-08: Decision point: rollback / continue (Slack #releases)
- 2026-03-09: Expand to 10% us-west1 + 2% eu-west1 11:00-11:30 PT (owner: Diego)
- 2026-03-11: Midpoint metrics write-up (owner: Priya)
- 2026-03-12: Expand to 25% global stagger (owner: release-engineering rotation)
- 2026-03-18: Final decision; start full rollout if green

Preflight Checklist (must pass before any prod canary):
- [ ] Staging smoke: generation + chat flows exercise (>95% success across sample prompts).
- [ ] Perf bench: 1k synthetic requests at median sequence length to validate latency delta <= +8%.
- [ ] Cost projection: run Optimize simulator (sample workload) and confirm per-token cost change < 3%.
- [ ] KV cache sanity: validate no cache eviction regressions on long-chat scenario.
- [ ] Telemetry toggle: can be turned off via config; test toggle flip in staging.
- [ ] Rollback image ready: tag v1.3.1-rollback and tested for immediate redeploy.
- [ ] Pager duty rota updated and on-call notified (assign to release-owner).
- [ ] Post-release smoke playbook attached to the release ticket.

Canary Deploy Steps (detailed):
1) Pre-deploy (T-60m):
   - Announce in #releases and #oncall Slack channels with exact time and expected window.
   - Reconfirm PD coverage and oncall escalation path.
   - Confirm canary traffic target and routing policy in rollout config.
2) Deploy (T-0):
   - Push canary traffic policy; deploy runtime v1.3.2 to canary pool (Samir).
   - Tag terraform/infra change if any and run quick plan (no infra changes expected).
3) Immediate smoke (T+5m):
   - Run smoke harness against canary endpoints: sample chat gen, streaming, embeddings.
   - Post results to the release ticket.
4) Monitoring window (T+0 to T+6h):
   - Watch dashboards (see thresholds below).
   - Notify channel every hour with short snapshot.
5) Decision (T+6h):
   - If green: continue hold or expand per calendar.
   - If threshold breached: rollback and file an incident (see rollback criteria).

Primary Dashboards & Thresholds (gates):
- Latency P95 (99 for long contexts): must not increase > 15% relative to baseline.
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) overall: absolute < 0.5% and no region > 1.5%
- Token generation failure modes: missing tokens / truncation events < 0.1%
- Cost per 1k tokens (proxy): expected delta within +/- 5% (investigate if outside)
- Queue depth / backpressure metric: no sustained increase > 20%
- New telemetry events: confirm expected event volume matches sample estimate (toggle instrumentation)

Rollback Criteria (explicit):
- Any sustained P95 latency regression > 20% for 30+ minutes.
- Sudden error spike > 1.5% regionally or > 0.75% global for 15+ minutes.
- Any customer-facing regression detected in CS tickets or increased 1-on-1 complaints (triaged as Sev2+).
- Telemetry toggle misfires (duplicate events or missing fields).

Rollback Procedure (fast):
- Notify Slack: "Rolling back v1.3.2 canary in <region> due to <metric>".
- Trigger automated rollback job (infra: redeploy image v1.3.1-rollback to affected pool).
- Clear canary traffic policy and set traffic -> 0% to canary pool.
- Run post-rollback smoke and capture metrics for forensics.
- Open an incident with initial notes and assign to primary engineer.

Communication Plan (templates):
- Pre-deploy announcement (Slack):
  "Deploying runtime v1.3.2 (micro-canary) to 2% us-west1 at 09:00 PT. Owners: Samir (deploy), Priya (observability). If you see regressions, ping @oncall and #releases. Linked ticket: REL-6789"
- Hourly status update (short):
  "[09:00-10:00] Canary us-west1 2% — P95 +2%, errors 0.12%, no action"
- Rollback notice:
  "Rolling back v1.3.2 canary in us-west1 — error rate crossed threshold. Rolling to v1.3.1-rollback. Incident: <link>"

Post-release verification (after any expansion):
- Run 3 representative prompt sets and store outputs for quality regression analysis (owner: Hannah).
- Export cost telemetry for the canary cohort and run comparison vs baseline.
- Confirm no new warnings in runtime logs related to kernel selections or quantization fallbacks.
- Update canary notes in release ticket with a short summary and attach graphs.

Draft Release Notes (candidate blurb for customers/internal):
- Runtime v1.3.2 (rolling): Improved batching heuristics to reduce average latency for short chats; added optional telemetry toggle for more granular instrumentation.
- Expected impact: small latency improvements for short sequences; negligible functional changes.
- Rollout: gradual canary, will monitor for regressions and rollback if necessary.

Known unknowns / open questions:
- Are there any customers pinned to older model variants that may observe a different routing outcome? (action: product to confirm)
- Does the telemetry toggle double-count any custom customer events? (action: Diego to validate against sample events)
- Should we include a customer-facing note in account emails ahead of the rollout? (tentative: no unless any functional change)

Postmortem readiness notes (if rollback happens):
- Collect logs + KV cache traces for the canary window (retain for 30 days).
- Export detailed A/B traffic slice to S3 (path: s3://redwood-release/rel-6789/canary-slices/).
- Keep release ticket open until final RCA and verification are posted.

Quick TODOs (owner tags):
- [Priya] Finish staging smoke harness and post results (by 2026-03-03).
- [Samir] Create canary traffic policy and verify deploy script (by 2026-03-04).
- [Diego] Validate telemetry toggle in staging with sample event set (by 2026-03-03).
- [Hannah] Prep quality prompt sets and evaluate outputs after each expansion (ongoing).

Notes to self: this is intentionally slim — aim for speed and measurability. If any gate trips, escalations should be automatic and the rollback path should be the default.

-- end of draft --

(If this doc looks good, I'll convert to the formal release brief and attach the baseline graphs + synthetic bench tarball before the rollout.)
